definition: A tool that detects copied or AI-generated text — increasingly unreliable at distinguishing AI from human writing.
details: A tool that detects copied or AI-generated text — increasingly unreliable at distinguishing AI from human writing.

explainer.lead: An AI plagiarism checker examines writing for copied material, AI-generated text, or both. It can help reviewers decide where to look more closely, but an AI-authorship flag is not dependable proof that a person did not write the text.

tiers.eli5: It is like a school helper who compares your essay with other writing and sometimes guesses whether a computer wrote it. The comparison can point out matching passages, but the guess about computer writing can be wrong. A person still needs to check before making an accusation.
tiers.practitioner: Use these checkers as screening aids in document-review workflows, keeping copied-passage findings separate from AI-authorship assessments. Do not treat an AI label as conclusive evidence: require human review before consequential decisions, because distinguishing AI-generated text from human writing is increasingly unreliable.
tiers.paperLevel: For text t, a checker may provide a copying assessment C(t), an AI-authorship assessment A(t), or both; these are distinct tasks rather than interchangeable measures. A central limitation is the increasing unreliability of A(t) in distinguishing AI-generated text from human writing, so its output cannot by itself establish authorship.

explainer.example: A student submits an essay, and the checker highlights a sentence copied from an article while also labeling another paragraph as AI-generated. The reviewer can compare the highlighted sentence with the article, but the AI label alone does not show who wrote the paragraph.

usedIn.name: Education
usedIn.detail: Reviewers can screen student writing for copied passages or possible AI-generated text before examining the work themselves.

usedIn.name: Publishing
usedIn.detail: Editorial teams can use a report as an initial prompt for closer review of submitted writing.

usedIn.name: Academic integrity
usedIn.detail: Staff can use findings to guide an investigation rather than as standalone proof of misconduct.

explainer.intuition: Checking for copying and guessing whether text was AI-generated are different questions. The first concerns overlap with existing material; the second concerns authorship, and its results should be treated cautiously.
howItWorks: A person submits a piece of writing to the checker.
The tool looks for copied material, possible AI-generated text, or both.
It returns findings for the reviewer to inspect.
The reviewer checks any copied passages and treats AI-authorship labels as uncertain.
A person makes the final decision using more than the AI label alone.
explainer.whyItMatters: These tools can focus human attention during writing review, but unreliable authorship judgments can lead to unfair accusations. Separating evidence of copying from uncertain AI detection helps keep decisions grounded.
misconceptions: AI-generated text and plagiarized text are the same thing.
An AI-detection flag proves that a person did not write the text.
A clean result proves that writing is both original and human-written.
